<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# ⚠️ Warning: Availability Gate Failed

**The availability gate is not met.** Measured availability is **99.1%**, below the 99.5% threshold by **0.4 percentage points**. Over a 7-day week (10,080 minutes), that is about **40 minutes** more downtime than allowed (roughly 91 minutes actual vs. a 50-minute budget).

The incident-duration gate **passed**.

---

# Weekly Availability Summary

| Gate | Threshold | Measured | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | ≥ 99.5% | 99.1% | ❌ **Fail** (short by 0.4 pp) |
| Max single incident | ≤ 60 min | 41 min | ✅ Pass (19 min under limit) |

**Incidents**
- Incident 1: 12 minutes
- Incident 2: 41 minutes
- Total incident time: 53 minutes

**Note on a discrepancy:** If the measurement covers a full 7-day week, 99.1% availability means about 91 minutes of downtime. The two recorded incidents account for only 53 minutes. That leaves about 38 minutes unexplained. Possible causes include unlogged incidents, partial or degraded outages counted against availability, planned maintenance, or a measurement window shorter than a full week. It would be worth checking this, since the 53 recorded minutes alone would have passed the 99.5% gate (about 99.47% would still fall just short, so the gate fails either way).

**Overall status: Not met.** Availability is below target, though no individual incident breached the 60-minute limit.
